ram_free_source: Runner RSS 11.1 GB in the full-speed runs bench/results/llamacpp-20261015-100648.jsonl and -101143.jsonl (4K); at 7.4 GB RSS the 60K speed fell from 38.2 to 9.7 tok/s.
cache_ram_source: llama-server's default 8192 MiB host-RAM prompt cache pushed 8.7 GB of the 35B server into swap during a long interactive session on 16 GB RAM; --cache-ram 2048 completed the 6-model, 96-run comparison without swap growth.

measured.source: Performance with the exact launch configuration (ctx 65536, profile server_args): bench/results/llamacpp-20261017-234751.jsonl. Quality: bench/results/quality-20261015-014745.jsonl (server context/args not recorded).

ram_pressure.note: With less free RAM the 13 GB model drops out of the page cache (runner RSS 11.1 -> 7.4 GB, NVMe reads up to 626 MB/s) and deep-context speed collapses. 32 GB RAM is recommended for long contexts.

measured.notes: 4K speed is stable across three launch-config runs (46.5 / 48.1 / 49.7 tok/s); 32K/60K speed depends on free RAM. At ctx 33792 the same flags reached 53.6 / 48.5 tok/s (bench/results/llamacpp-20261015-023913.jsonl) because the smaller KV cache leaves more VRAM for experts. MTP n=2 +14 % TG @4K, +10 % @32K vs. no MTP (ctx 33792 runs). --moe-cache-mib 1024 measured slower on 8 GB and is off.
measured.note_128k: 128K works (120K prompt: 25.0 t/s TG, 543 t/s PP, ~3.7 min to first token) but is too slow as a default
